name: Wang Zhenjian
current_role: Chairman, Chongqing Shunbo Aluminum Co., Ltd. (顺博合金, SZSE: 002996)
profile: Wang Zhenjian (王真见, b. 1964) is chairman and co-controlling shareholder (~20.5%) of Shunbo Aluminum, one of China's top-four recycled aluminium alloy producers, with plants in Chongqing, Qingyuan, Liyang, Xiangyang and Anhui. He has 30+ years in scrap-metal recycling; the company listed in Shenzhen in Aug 2020.
interesting_fact: Shunbo is a pure recycled-aluminium (circular-economy) business: it turns scrap aluminium into alloy ingots for auto and motorcycle parts, and produced ~553,000 tonnes of alloy ingot in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shunbo he worked at the Xilu metal fittings factory in Yongkang, Zhejiang, then ran the Xilu metal processing plant in Chongqing's Jiulongpo district as factory director; he was vice-chairman of Shunbo Ltd from 2008 and chairman since May 2013.
notes: Low public profile; no personal media presence found. Controls company jointly with Wang Zengchao and Wang Qi. Best route is the board secretary via ir@sballoy.com (Chinese-language).

He was chief engineer of the TV products division and chaired CVTE's supervisory board from 2011; CVTE (Seewo, MAXHUB brands) listed in Shenzhen in 2017. He no longer appears among current officers but remains a top-10 shareholder.

deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding CVTE he worked as an engineer at Amoi (Xiaxin Electronics), Guangzhou Lehua Electronics and Guangzhou Chixun, then joined CVTE at its founding as deputy chief engineer of the TV products division.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal media/social accounts found. Only route is via CVTE board office (shiyuan@cvte.com). Not to be confused with other people named Ren Rui.

name: Victor Perlroth
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Kodiak Sciences Inc. (Nasdaq: KOD), Palo Alto
profile: Victor Perlroth, M.D. (Princeton A.B. molecular biology; Stanford M.D./M.B.A.) co-founded Kodiak Sciences in 2009 and leads it as chairman and CEO, developing long-acting retinal drugs for wet AMD and diabetic eye disease. He earlier co-founded Avidia, sold to Amgen for $450m, then worked in life-sciences venture capital.

deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was chief operating officer of Guzik Technical Enterprises, a maker of test equipment for the hard-disk-drive industry; he graduated summa cum laude from Princeton in molecular biology.

name: Michael Douglas
current_role: Actor and film producer (announced retirement from acting in 2025); UN Messenger of Peace; board member, Nuclear Threat Initiative
profile: Michael Douglas (b. 1944), son of Kirk Douglas, won Best Picture as producer of One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and Best Actor as Gordon Gekko in Wall Street. Listed with wife Catherine Zeta-Jones on the UK rich list; his wealth comes from acting and producing. He is a long-time nuclear-disarmament advocate.

name: David Crossland
current_role: Jersey-based private investor; founder and former chairman of Airtours/MyTravel Group
profile: David Crossland (b. 1946), from east Lancashire, founded Airtours in 1972 by buying two small travel shops in Nelson, then built it into MyTravel, a global package-holiday group with its own charter airline, which merged with Thomas Cook AG in 2007. He now lives in Jersey and invests privately (travel and investment per the rich list).
interesting_fact: Airtours' first two shops (Pendle Travel Services, Nelson) were bought from an elderly couple, with half the money borrowed from his brother-in-law; Airtours later launched its own airline in 1990 and offered £299 Caribbean charters.
deep_cut_fact: He left Burnley Grammar School with three O-levels and his first job, in August 1963, was at the travel agency inside the Colne Co-operative Society's Colne Hall offices on Albert Road, where he learnt the trade.
notes: Private; no published personal/office contact found (web search budget ran out mid-lane, so current business interests were not re-verified). Alive status assumed from no death record on Wikipedia.

name: Anastasios Gianakakos
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chair, Kardigan, Inc. (Nasdaq: KARD), South San Francisco

name: Raju Vegesna
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Sify Technologies Ltd (Nasdaq: SIFY), Chennai
profile: Raju Vegesna is a serial chip and systems entrepreneur: he founded ServerWorks (x86 server chipsets, sold to Broadcom for $1.8bn in 2001) and ServerEngines (sold to Emulex in 2010). He bought control of Indian ICT provider Sify in 2005 via Infinity Capital Ventures and chairs it; Sify runs networks, cloud and data centres across India.
interesting_fact: ServerWorks, which he founded in 1994, held about 90% of the x86 server chipset market before Broadcom bought it for $1.8bn; he now leads Sify, a major Indian data-centre and network operator.
deep_cut_fact: As a Motorola engineer he wrote the microcode for the 68030 processor and the specification for the 68040; at Ross Technology he was chief architect of the HyperSPARC CPU used in Sun's first multiprocessor servers.
notes: Strong fit for a data-centre podcast (Sify is a large Indian DC operator). Also funds the Raju Vegesna Foundation (clean water and education). Hurun lists him under India though he built his career in Silicon Valley.
